inputs.share_count_basis: 2,613.4m shares in issue ex-treasury after the 20 Oct 2026 issue of 20.55m consideration shares (HKEX completion announcement 2026-10-20; 2,592.9m at 30 Sep 2026 monthly return), plus ~13.6m net dilution from the in-the-money options (10.4m @0.875, 8.0m @1.02, 22.9m @2.18; FY2025 AR note 30, treasury-stock method at the current price). The 124.3m options struck at HK$5.00-8.70 are out of the money and excluded. The proposed HK$530m CB converts at HK$3.02 (175.5m shares) and is carried as DEBT, not shares, because the conversion price is above both the market price and every scenario IV below HK$3.02; if the stock trades through 3.02 the count rises ~6.7% and net debt falls HK$530m, roughly a wash. Count held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (0.5% of revenue).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim: bank loans 401.5 current + 62.4 non-current = 463.8; zero-coupon CB at redemption principal 1,458.0 (carrying 1,438.4; redeemed at principal 28 Sep 2026); cash 896.5 (restricted cash 10.2 excluded). Lease liabilities 17.6 EXCLUDED (treatment B, lease cash charged in the flows). The CB redemption on 28 Sep 2026 consumed the cash pile plus bridge borrowings and the 21 Oct 2026 HK$530m 3.75% CB due 25 Oct 2027 refinances 'existing indebtedness' -- net debt is unchanged in substance, its composition shifts from a zero-coupon CB to bank loans + a 3.75% coupon CB. H2 FY2026 operating cash burn since 30 June is not yet disclosed and is not in this figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share compensation expense' HK$18,720k (and the Adjusted Net Profit reconciliation, same figure); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (net-share settlement not used). H1 FY2026 interim: HK$4,842k.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income HK$16.0m is stripped from the FCF base although the company is net-debt: the HK$1,157m year-end cash pile (time deposits raised by the Sep 2025 CB) is credited in full in the net-debt bridge and was consumed by the Sep 2026 redemption, so its income cannot also sit in the flows (matching-asset rule). The forward build is EBITDA-based and carries no interest income.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 nil; H1 FY2026 HK$12.5m purchased by the share-award-plan trustee (4.3m shares) -- funding of the award plan, not a count reduction. The flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for; historically the count has grown ~45% FY2020-FY2025 through CB conversions, placements and acquisition shares, all non-SBC issuance that is now charged as debt or is in the current count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows discounted at an HKD-built rate: 10-year HKSAR government bond ~3.6% (USD-pegged), ERP 5.5%, beta 1.4 for a HK$6-7bn small-cap with ~50% Chinese Mainland revenue and a 52-week range of 2.17-6.30 -> cost of equity ~11.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (3.75% CB coupon, SOFR-plus bank loans); ~85/15 equity/debt -> WACC ~10.3%, rounded to 10.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- receivable quality, refinancing and the unproven AI pivot are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked onto the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (FY2025 HK$12.3m + 0.8m = 13.1m, 0.46% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path 0.45%; lease liabilities (HK$17.6m at 30 Jun 2026) excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 PP&E 15.7m + intangibles 140.6m = 156.3m, 5.4% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 30 June 2026 book value HK$229.2m (Particle Technology minority, 38.82%); flows are modelled on the consolidated basis. The call option to buy out that 38.82% for RMB542m (FVTPL carrying HK$156.6m at FY2025) is excluded from the bridge: exercising it costs cash roughly equal to the stake it acquires.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 1-2: operating company, non-US, with the adaptations file applied -- HKD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI charged once, matching-asset rule for the wealth-management products). Vobile is a B2B digital-content-protection and rights-monetisation company (subscription 43% / revenue-share value-added 57%), not a financial or property business, so the flows are the right object. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year end); FY2026 is forecast year 1, anchored on H1 FY2026 actuals (revenue +24%, adjusted EBITDA margin 19.1%). THE CENTRAL ISSUE IN THIS VALUATION IS CASH CONVERSION, NOT PROFIT: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA HK$542m converted to HK$71m cash from operations because trade receivables rose HK$377m and prepayments HK$203m -- working capital absorbed ~99% of the HK$471m revenue increase in FY2025 and ~100% in FY2024, ~57% in H1 FY2026. Trade receivables stand at HK$1,915m, ~60% of TTM revenue (DSO ~215 days), with HK$26.8m of ECL impairment in FY2025. On top of that, HK$428m of FY2025 'capex' is capitalised development and purchased copyright/software (capitalised development carrying value 499m vs 200m a year earlier), and H1 FY2026 added HK$183m of PP&E (AI compute for DreamMaker). Reported FCF has been negative every year since FY2021 and owner FCF was -HK$398m in FY2025. The model therefore charges working capital as a negative capture on the revenue CHANGE in every scenario, lets capex converge onto D&A only over 6-7 years, and treats the Sep 2025 HK$1.6bn zero-coupon CB as debt at its redemption principal. POST-BALANCE-SHEET EVENTS (HKEX announcements, read 2026-10-23): 28 Sep 2026 full cash redemption of the HK$1,458m CB at principal; 9/20 Oct 2026 acquisition of an AI digital-watermarking company for HK$75m in 20.55m shares at HK$3.65; 21 Oct 2026 proposed HK$530m 3.75% CB due 25 Oct 2027, conversion HK$3.02, 'for repayment of existing indebtedness' -- i.e. the refinancing rolls a 12-month zero-coupon into a 12-month 3.75% coupon, so the company remains on a one-year funding cycle. Price is the HKEX regular close; not an after-hours print. Equity bridge adds the bank/non-bank wealth-management products held at FVTPL (cash-like, their FV gains are outside adjusted EBITDA) and deducts NCI at book.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim statement of financial position; NCI charged once here, flows consolidated

FVTPL total 425.7 less the Particle Technology call option (~157.7, FY2025 note 22 basis); FY2025 unlisted investments were 261.8. Matching-asset rule: FV gains on these are excluded from adjusted EBITDA, so the asset is added at carrying value. May already have been liquidated to fund the Sep 2026 CB redemption, in which case it is cash that reduced debt -- same answer.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 year-1 growth anchored on H1 FY2026 revenue +24% YoY and FY2025 +19.6%, decelerating to 3% terminal over 10 years; the historical equity CAGR is not usable as a growth proxy (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (29-33%) is driven by share issuance (CB conversions, the 2025 placement, acquisition shares: count +45% FY2020-FY2025), not retained earnings, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 53% includes the 2021-22 ZEFR/Particle acquisitions. Neither is an organic growth signal. Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF was negative in every year FY2020-FY2025 (-2.0, -144.0, -124.6, -146.3, -249.3, -398.2 HK$m), and became more negative as revenue grew -- the series says growth has consumed cash, not produced it.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income, all years: FY2020 22.2-24.0-0.2; FY2021 -75.1-67.4-1.6; FY2022 -67.5-52.6-4.5; FY2023 -100.0-41.9-4.4; FY2024 -220.8-24.3-4.2; FY2025 -363.4-18.7-16.0. SBC fell from 7.1% of revenue (FY2020) to 0.65% (FY2025) while reported FCF deteriorated, so the SBC adjustment is no longer the reason the owner series is negative -- working capital and capitalised development are.

base.wc_capture_rationale: Working capital absorbed ~99% of the FY2025 revenue increase and ~100% of FY2024's, 57% in H1 FY2026. Receivables are ~60% of TTM revenue. A single -45% capture over the horizon assumes collections improve from the H1 FY2026 pace toward ~40% of incremental revenue as the revenue-share platform settlements mature -- better than the last three years, worse than any normal software business.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin 18.9% FY2025, 19.1% H1 FY2026; year 1 starts at 18.5% because the ~0.9%-of-revenue ECL charge on receivables (FY2025 HK$26.8m) is treated as a recurring cost rather than a non-IFRS add-back. Matures to 22% on gross-margin stability (44.8-44.9%) and S&M/admin leverage; note that ~10% of revenue of R&D is capitalised, which flatters EBITDA and is charged back through capex.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2025 capex 15.1% of revenue (intangibles 14.9%), H1 FY2026 20.6% (PP&E 10.1% for AI compute + intangibles 10.4%). Converges to 10% by year 7 as DreamMaker compute build-out completes; D&A ex-ROU rises from 5.4% toward 9.8% as the HK$499m of capitalised development amortises -- terminal capex ~ D&A + growth.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes paid 6.6% of PBT (US tax losses being utilised: deferred tax asset for losses down to HK$9.6m, so the shelter is nearly exhausted; deferred tax liabilities rising on capitalised development). Ramps to 20% blended (HK 16.5%, PRC 15-25%, US 21%+state) by year 5.

scenario_narratives.base: AI-era content volume keeps both the subscription (monitoring) and value-added (revenue-share) lines growing -- FY2026 +22% off H1's +24%, fading to mid-single digits by year 7 as the short-drama and music (Pex) tailwinds mature and platforms' in-house Content-ID keeps the price of third-party identification in check. Adjusted EBITDA margin edges from 19% to 22% on gross-margin stability and S&M leverage. The decisive assumptions are below the EBITDA line: working capital absorbs 45% of every incremental revenue dollar (collections improve from the ~100% of FY2024-25 but DSO stays well above 150 days), capex (capitalised R&D + AI compute) takes until year 7 to converge onto D&A at ~10% of revenue, and cash tax normalises to 20% as the US loss shelter runs out. Owner FCF is negative for the first three forecast years and reaches a ~9% margin only by year 10, so most of the value is terminal. DreamMaker/SeeBay/RWA are carried as upside options, not as modelled revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-copyright thesis works: regulatory consensus on licensed use of copyrighted material for generative AI (US/EU/PRC legislation now advancing), element-level identification and the Pex music catalogue push growth to 26%/24%/21% and the value-added mix shift plus DreamMaker compute revenue (>US$10m in its first half) lift adjusted EBITDA margin to 26%. Crucially, platform settlement cycles shorten and receivables stop compounding: working capital captures only 30% of incremental revenue, and the AI-compute build-out ends by year 5 with capex at 9%. Terminal growth 3.5% capped at 20x. This is the case the Sep 2025 CB buyers at HK$5.87 and the Crédit Agricole HK$7.6 target were underwriting.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth stalls at 15% then low single digits as YouTube/Chinese-platform in-house identification commoditises monitoring, AI-rights frameworks settle in a way that bypasses third-party settlement, and short-drama/UGC monetisation economics soften. Margins slip to 16% on pricing and R&D that can no longer be capitalised at the same rate. The receivables book (HK$1.9bn, 60% of revenue, HK$27m ECL in FY2025) proves the profit was never cash: working capital absorbs 55% of what little revenue growth there is, and capex only falls to 9% -- barely above D&A -- leaving a business that cannot generate owner FCF materially above zero. With HK$1.0bn of net debt rolled on a 12-month cycle (the HK$1.458bn CB was redeemed in cash in Sep 2026 and immediately refinanced with a 3.75% CB due Oct 2027), the equity is worth little or nothing on this path; expect the engine to show this scenario at or near the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the downside is not a margin story but a cash-conversion and refinancing story: owner FCF has been negative for six straight years, receivables are 60% of revenue, and the company has just rolled a 12-month zero-coupon CB into a 12-month 3.75% CB after a redemption that consumed its entire cash pile. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- AI-rights regulation landing favourably, DreamMaker/SeeBay/RWA scaling from a rounding error, and platform settlement cycles shortening so receivables stop absorbing growth. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Vobile reports rising profits (FY2025 net profit +34%, H1 FY2026 +93%) that have never arrived as cash: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of HK$542m became HK$71m of operating cash and -HK$363m of reported free cash flow, because receivables and prepayments absorb essentially all incremental revenue and ~HK$430m a year of development and content is capitalised. The DCF is therefore built on components that charge those two drains explicitly -- a negative working-capital capture on the revenue change and capex converging onto D&A only by year 7 -- rather than on an EBITDA multiple or the company's adjusted net profit. The Sep 2025 HK$1.6bn CB is carried at its redeemed principal, NCI is deducted at book, the wealth-management products are added as cash-like, and the Oct 2026 HK$530m CB (conversion HK$3.02) is debt. Value lives almost entirely in the terminal year, when the model assumes the business finally converts ~9% of revenue to owner cash; the price today is paying for AI-copyright optionality (DreamMaker, SeeBay, RWA tokenisation, the Ant Digital copyright-model collaboration) that the base case carries at zero.
key_risks_to_valuation: Receivable quality: HK$1.9bn of trade receivables (~215 days of revenue) with the ECL charge tripling in FY2025 -- a collection shortfall or write-down converts reported profit into a loss and the model's -45% capture would be too generous

Refinancing cycle: net debt ~HK$1.0bn, the Sep 2026 redemption consumed the cash pile, and the replacement is a 12-month 3.75% CB due 25 Oct 2027 -- a second failed conversion forces another cash redemption or a dilutive reset

Dilution outside SBC: 175.5m shares if the new CB converts at HK$3.02, 20.5m consideration shares just issued, and a track record of placements and CB conversions (+45% count FY2020-25); the flat count assumes no further non-SBC issuance

Capitalised development (HK$499m carrying value) and purchased copyright are judgment-heavy intangibles; a change in capitalisation policy or impairment would collapse EBITDA margin without changing cash
Platform in-house identification (YouTube Content ID, Chinese platforms) and an AI-rights legal settlement that bypasses third-party settlement would cap both growth and pricing
Chinese Mainland is ~50% of revenue: data/content regulation and RMB translation
Terminal-value dependence: owner FCF is negative through year 3 in the base case, so the valuation is a bet on cash conversion that has not yet been demonstrated
